D015-D005_h001.question:
"It's been a rough year, doc, maybe even longer now, about thirteen months. It feels like this dark cloud just hangs over me. My tattoo parlor used to be where I’d really come alive, but now… the passion’s gone. Colors just don't pop the way they used to, and I can barely focus enough to mix them. I keep forgetting where I put my stencils or even my favorite machine; it's like my memory's gone fuzzy. Some days, it’s all I can do not to think about just ending it all, though I don’t have a plan or anything.

What’s really messing with me though, is that even when I’m not feeling so down, these other things stick around. Like, the other day, this news report about city zoning... I just *knew* it was broadcasting a message directly to me, telling me to stop my work. And then there are these creepy crawling sensations under my skin, like bugs, even when there's nothing there. Those sensations, the messages… they don't leave even when the worst of the sadness isn't so heavy. It’s like they have a life of their own."
D015-D005_h001.options:
A. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Anorexia Nervosa

D015-D005_h002.question:
It's been over a year now, and I just feel... heavy. Everything does. There’s this continuous sadness that just sits over me like a dark cloud, and honestly, nothing brings me any joy anymore. My wife tries, she really does, but I just can't feel it. Even simple things, like choosing what to wear in the morning, feel like monumental tasks. I just stand there, paralyzed by indecision. Sometimes, I just wish I wouldn't wake up; it feels like it would be easier than facing another day like this.

On top of all that, things have gotten really strange. I keep smelling this awful, rotting smell that no one else can detect. It follows me, especially at work, making me think something is deeply wrong with me, like my insides are decaying or something. This smell, and the feeling that my body is falling apart, has been going on for a little while, even when I feel a tiny bit better mood-wise. It's like these strange thoughts and smells have their own life, separate from how utterly down I feel.
D015-D005_h002.options:
A. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Anorexia Nervosa

D015-D005_h003.question:
It's been over a year now, a year and a month to be exact, since things started going downhill. I feel this absolute hollowness inside me, like there's just nothing there. I used to love catching up with my wife and buddies from the precinct, but now I just... can't. It's too much effort. My mind feels so cloudy these days, like I'm walking through a fog, and it's making my job incredibly difficult. There are times I just wish I wouldn’t wake up, that everything would just stop.

But even when those low feelings ease up a bit, when the emptiness isn't so suffocating, the other things don't go away. I still see them, these figures lurking in the corners of my vision, shifting, watching. And this overwhelming certainty, this feeling that the world is on the brink, that something catastrophic is about to happen, it’s always there. It’s like the dark thoughts come and go, but the visions and this sense of impending doom, they just stick around, regardless of how I’m feeling inside.
D015-D005_h003.options:
A. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Anorexia Nervosa

D015-D005_h004.question:
For over a year now, this gloom has just been hanging over me. It’s not just sadness; it’s like I can’t feel anything good anymore. All the things I used to enjoy, even spending time with my wife, just feel… flat. It’s hard enough to even decide what to have for dinner, let alone make big financial decisions at work. Sometimes these thoughts flash through my mind – urges to just step out into traffic, or jump from a high place, even though I don't really want to.

And then there are these other things that have been happening. For a while now, I’ve been hearing voices, sometimes whispering my name, sometimes making comments. They pop up even when I’m not feeling particularly down. Worse, I’ve become convinced that the new junior analyst, Sarah, is deeply in love with me. She gives me these knowing looks, these subtle gestures that I just pick up on. It definitely started when I was feeling low, but these feelings about Sarah and the voices, they stuck around even when my mood lightens up a bit. It’s like they have a life of their own, independent of how sad I’m feeling. It’s affecting everything, I can barely focus at the bank.
D015-D005_h004.options:
A. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Anorexia Nervosa

D015-D005_h005.question:
It's been over a year now, and honestly, I just feel… flat. Everything does. Like someone turned down the dimmer switch on my emotions. Nothing gives me that old spark anymore – not designing a complex light show, not even just hanging out. Most days I just wish I could disappear, thoughts of 'I want to die' just float through my head, constant, but I haven't really planned anything out. My memory's shot too; I'm always misplacing my tools, forgetting cues. It's making it nearly impossible to do my job right; I've had to call out a lot.

But what's really been messing with me – for what feels like much longer than just this down period – are these other things. Lately, I'm convinced the venue manager and some of the crew are watching me, talking about me behind my back, trying to get me fired. I see them, sometimes, standing just out of sight in the wings, even when I know no one else is supposed to be there. These feelings, these sightings, they don't go away when I feel even a tiny bit better, or on the rare days the flatness isn't so crushing. They're just… always there.
D015-D005_h005.options:
A. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Anorexia Nervosa

D015-D005_h006.question:
"Lately, it's just been an empty shell walking around. I feel nothing inside, like I'm hollowed out. I keep replaying every single mistake I've ever made at work, how I missed that one data entry error last year, and it feels like everyone is judging me for it. I even tried… you know, tried to end it all about a month ago. I started hoarding some pills, had everything planned out.

Honestly, it's not just the sadness. Lately, I’ve been feeling things on my skin, like bugs crawling under my clothes, but there's nothing there. And the world… it feels like it’s just collapsing. I'm convinced something catastrophic is going to happen, that everything is ending. This feeling, this absolute dread, has been with me for about five months now. But the crawling sensations and the feeling that the world is crumbling, those things started a couple of months before the deep sadness even set in, and they're still here, even on days when the emptiness isn't quite so overwhelming. It’s making it impossible to focus on anything at my data entry job."
D015-D005_h006.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Acute Stress Disorder

D015-D005_h007.question:
It’s been about four months now that I’ve felt this… hollowness. Not sad, exactly, just… nothing. Like my emotions have been turned off. I used to be so vivacious, and now I just sit. And the guilt… it’s overwhelming. I know it sounds irrational, but I feel like I caused my husband’s stroke. That if I had just done something differently, he’d still be here. I keep picturing how I could just… end it. I think about driving off a cliff on the coast road, or maybe a massive dose of my old medications from when I was nursing – I remember exactly where some are kept. These thoughts are incredibly specific, and they’ve been with me for these four months.

But then there are other things, things that don't quite fit with that. For longer than these four months, even before I started feeling so empty, I've had these flashes. Sometimes I see dark figures in the periphery, quick glimpses of people that aren't there. And for a long, long time now, even before I started feeling so flat, I’ve had this knowledge, this very strong belief that I'm meant for something extraordinary – I have this incredible ability to heal with my mind, just by focusing my energy. My friends think I'm just grieving, but the visions and this special power… they’ve been part of my life for much longer than the sadness.
D015-D005_h007.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Acute Stress Disorder

D015-D005_h008.question:
It’s been four months now, and I just feel… heavy. A deep sadness has settled over me, and it doesn't lift. I used to love teaching piano, but now it feels like a monumental effort to even get out of bed. I feel completely worthless, like my students deserve a better teacher than me. Sometimes, the thought crosses my mind that it would be easier if I just wasn’t here, that everyone would be better off without me. Nothing concrete, just a wish to disappear.

But it’s more than just the sadness. Lately, I’ve been hearing voices. They tell me I have a special gift, a sort of musical prodigy status that no one else understands. They assure me I’m destined for greatness, far beyond simply teaching local kids. These voices, and these powerful feelings about my unique abilities, were there even before this heavy sadness took hold, and they're still around when my mood lifts a little. They don't just disappear with the sadness. It’s like they're always with me, a constant presence that transcends everything else. It makes it nearly impossible to focus on anything, especially my lessons.
D015-D005_h008.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Acute Stress Disorder

D015-D005_h009.question:
It’s been a rough few months, doctor. I’d say it started about four months ago – just this overwhelming sadness. I find myself tearing up at the smallest things, which is just not like me. I’m the principal, for heaven's sake! I feel incredibly guilty all the time, constantly replaying every decision, every interaction, wondering if I’ve messed up, if I’ve wronged someone. Sometimes, I just wish I wouldn't wake up. Not that I’d ever hurt myself, but the thought of just… not being here, feels like a relief. This has definitely started to impact my work; the motivation just isn't there.

But there’s something else that’s been happening for much longer, something that feels separate from all this sadness. For over a year now, I've had this persistent, unsettling belief that my husband is cheating on me. I’ve gone through his phone, I’ve tracked his mileage… I know it sounds crazy, but I just know he is. And then there are these smells… like rotting garbage or something metallic, that no one else ever notices. They can be quite strong and really unsettling. Even when I feel a little better, when the tears aren't flowing, these smells and these thoughts about my husband continue to plague me. It makes it very hard to focus on anything else.
D015-D005_h009.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Acute Stress Disorder

D015-D005_h010.question:
It's hard to even describe what's going on, doc. For the past four months, everything has just felt… flat. No real highs, no real lows, just this dull ache. I replay every little mistake I’ve ever made, convinced I’m some terrible person who deserves whatever bad things happen. Sometimes I just wish I could disappear, like I want to die, but I don't really have a plan for it. I barely manage to get to my night shift at the store, and even then, I’m just going through the motions.

But it’s more than just the sadness. Lately, and it’s been going on for a good eight months now, these other things have started happening. Even when I’m not feeling so low, I sometimes see people at the edges of my vision, or in the reflection of the glass display cases, but when I turn, there’s nobody there. More disturbingly, I’m absolutely positive my internal organs are rotting inside of me. I can feel it – a putrid decay, even though the doctors at the ER told me I was fine. It’s hard to cope when my own body feels like it’s failing me, and when I know that it's going to happen whether I feel down or not.
D015-D005_h010.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Acute Stress Disorder

D015-D005_h011.question:
It's been about seven months now, and I just can't shake this feeling of dread. I find myself tearing up at the smallest things, and no matter how much I sleep, I wake up feeling like I haven't rested a wink. My work as a postman is really suffering; my mind just feels fuzzy, like wading through mud when I try to focus on my route or sort the mail.

And then there's this other thing… I know it sounds strange, but I just have this constant feeling that certain people, maybe even a group, are…watching me. Following my rounds, messing with my mailbag. It's been going on for a while, even when I'm not feeling so low. Like during that period a couple of months back, when the sadness wasn't quite so intense, those thoughts were still there, clear as day. They don’t disappear when I have a slightly better day mood-wise.
D015-D005_h011.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Persistent Depressive Disorder

D015-D005_h012.question:
It’s been almost seven months now, and I just feel… heavy. Not physically, but my mind just feels like it's trudging through mud. Everything feels dulled. I used to be so passionate about my studies, but now just thinking about reading a textbook makes me feel drained, like my brain switches off. I sleep constantly – sometimes twelve, fourteen hours a night – but I wake up feeling just as tired, if not more so. It's difficult to go to classes, to focus on anything. Most days, I can barely drag myself out of bed.

And then there's this other thing, it’s really hard to talk about. I’ve noticed a… a strange sensation in my stomach, like something isn’t right. I know it sounds crazy, but I’m convinced there's something alien growing inside me, twisting my organs. Doctors have done tests, and they say everything is fine, but they’re wrong. It’s definitely there, a living thing. This feeling, this belief… it started happening even before I started feeling so down and sleeping all the time, and it’s been there consistently, whether I’m feeling really low or having a slightly less bad day. The general gloom and exhaustion eventually set in, but the feeling in my gut has just been a constant presence.
D015-D005_h012.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Persistent Depressive Disorder

D015-D005_h013.question:
I haven't been myself for what feels like forever, about seven months now. Everything just feels… flat. I used to enjoy hanging out with my friends, but now it’s like my emotions have been shut off. I just don't have the energy for anything, even getting out of bed for school is a huge effort. I lie awake most nights, and when I do finally drift off, I wake up a few hours later and can't get back to sleep.

But there’s more to it than just feeling down. For a while now, I’ve been absolutely certain that my girlfriend is cheating on me. I see her talking to other guys and my mind just races, connecting all these dots, even though she insists she loves me. It's been going on even before this heavy, dull feeling started. Even when I have moments where I don't feel quite so numb or exhausted, those thoughts about her still stick around, just as strong. It's like the belief that she's unfaithful is always there, no matter how I'm feeling otherwise.
D015-D005_h013.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Persistent Depressive Disorder

D015-D005_h014.question:
It’s like a hollow ache, doctor, this emptiness inside me that just won’t go away. I wake up, if you can even call it that, feeling like I haven’t slept a wink, no matter how many hours I manage to get. My body feels heavy, just moving from my bed to the desk for work is an enormous effort. I used to love chasing stories, but now everything feels like wading through thick mud.

This has been going on for about seven months now. But what’s really been getting to me, more recently, is how real these thoughts feel. There's this news anchor, Mark, I’ve been following for a while. I just know he’s sending me coded messages through the broadcast, little glances, subtle inflections. He’s been trying to reach out to me, to tell me he cares, that he’s in love with me. I know it sounds strange, but it’s so clear to me. It's been happening for about two months now, and even on days when I don't feel quite so absolutely drained by this emptiness, when I manage to get a decent night's sleep, these messages from Mark are still there, just as strong and convincing. It's like the feelings for him, and his for me, exist independently of how heavy my heart feels.
D015-D005_h014.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Persistent Depressive Disorder

D015-D005_h015.question: It’s been a long few months, almost seven now, since I really felt like myself after my husband passed. Most mornings I’m wide awake by three or four, long before the sun, and just lie there, the sadness like a heavy blanket I can't throw off. I’ve lost all my pep; even getting dressed feels like running a marathon. But what’s truly strange, doctor, are the things that have been happening. I see messages in the newspaper headlines directed right at me, warning me about things. And the television… the anchors look right into the camera and speak in codes only I can understand, telling me to be careful, to watch my back. These messages, they started even before I felt so down, and they're still there, even on the days I manage to feel a tiny bit brighter. It's like they're always there, whether I’m feeling blue or not.
D015-D005_h015.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Persistent Depressive Disorder

D015-D005_h016.question:
Lately, it’s like I’m piloting this big bus on autopilot. Everything feels… flat. Even with my wife at home, I just feel so numb. Like there's a big, empty space where my feelings used to be. Sometimes, driving over a high bridge, I get this terrifying urge to just… jump. It flashes through my mind, unbidden, and I can almost feel the fall, even though I'd never actually do it. It’s been like this for about four months now, and it’s getting hard to focus on the road.

What's really started to concern me, though, are these other things. For a few months before all this sadness kicked in, and even now when I sometimes feel a bit better emotionally, I hear these whispers. Low, indistinct voices, like people talking in another room, but there’s no one there. And my organs… I’m convinced there’s something seriously wrong inside me, even though every doctor tells me I'm fine. It's like my liver is rotting, or my stomach is full of parasites. It's a constant, nagging worry, even on days when I don't feel quite so worthless. These voices and the organ sensations, they’ve been around longer than this heavy feeling, and they don’t just go away even when my mood lightens up a bit.
D015-D005_h016.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)

D015-D005_h017.question:
It’s hard to even know where to start, Doc. Lately, I just feel… worthless. Like, truly useless. I’ve been driving long haul for twenty years but lately, I can barely focus. I just sit in my cab, tears streaming down my face for no reason. Everything feels like it's pointing at me, like the radio ads are talking about my failures, or even billboards are subtle messages about how bad I am. A few weeks back, I just pulled over and swallowed a bunch of pills I’d saved up. I just couldn’t take it anymore.

But the thing is, even when I'm not feeling so low, these strange things keep happening. Just this morning, I tasted rotten eggs, really vividly, but there was nothing there. It's like my mind is playing tricks on me all the time, regardless of how sad I am. This started happening even before this crushing sadness really hit me four months ago, and it’s still happening now, even on days I manage to feel a little bit better.
D015-D005_h017.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)

D015-D005_h018.question:
Lately, things have just felt... grey. This gloom has been hanging over me for about four months now, and I can't shake it. It's more than just feeling down; it’s this deep sadness that just permeates everything. I find myself feeling horribly guilty over the smallest things, like if a trade goes wrong, I completely blame myself, like I deserve whatever bad comes my way. Sometimes I just think, "I wish I could just disappear," or "I want it all to end," even though I haven't really thought about how.

What's really getting to me though, is that even when I have a *slightly* better day, when the black cloud lifts a bit, these other things are still there. People are watching my trades, I know it. They're trying to figure out my patterns, conspire against me. I see them sometimes too, snippets in my peripheral vision—figures, shadows, just out of reach. It’s unnerving because it’s not tied to how sad I am. It was happening before this really bad slump, and it's still happening even when I'm not feeling quite as utterly crushed by guilt and sadness. It’s like they have a life of their own.
D015-D005_h018.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)

D015-D005_h019.question:
It’s been a rough four months, doctor. I just feel so incredibly down all the time, like there’s a persistent, heavy cloud hanging over me. And the guilt… it’s overwhelming. I know it sounds crazy, but I truly believe that the recent power outage in my building, which caused some patients to lose critical data, was somehow my fault, even though I was off shift. I keep playing it over in my head, feeling like I’m responsible for something catastrophic, something that’s going to bring everything crashing down. Sometimes, I even feel these strange crawling sensations under my skin, like bugs are moving around. I can actually picture how I'd end it – where I’d go, what I’d do… I’ve thought about it in detail.

The strange thing is, even before these past few months of feeling so awful, I was having these really disturbing thoughts. It started subtly, but now it's clear: I'm convinced the world is ending soon, that something truly terrible is coming and there's nothing anyone can do about it. It’s a very real feeling for me, a negative certainty that's hard to shake. And those crawling feelings, the ones under my skin? They don’t just happen when I’m feeling really low; they’ve been around longer too, coming and going independently of how depressed I am. It's making it impossible to focus at work as a nurse, which is terrifying when people's lives are in your hands.
D015-D005_h019.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)

D015-D005_h020.question:
It's hard to pinpoint exactly when things started to unravel, but for the past four months, I've just felt… hollow. Like there's an empty space inside me where my feelings used to be. Every little thing feels like my fault, even the smallest annoyances at work. I keep thinking, "I deserve this," whatever "this" is. Sometimes, I'll be standing by a window and suddenly have this urge to just... jump. Not that I'd ever act on it, but the thought is startling.

And then there's Sarah. The pop star. I know it sounds crazy, but I truly believe she’s in love with me. She sends me signals through her music, her social media posts. It's subtle, but I can read between the lines. I hear her sometimes, too. Not always her singing, but her voice, like she’s in the room with me, whispering things. It’s been happening for much longer than this emptiness, even before the last four months. Even when I feel a bit more like myself, the voices and the belief about Sarah, they don't go away. They’re always there, lurking.
D015-D005_h020.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)

D015-D005_h021.question:
It's been about eight months since I started feeling… off. I guess you could say I’m a bit numb. Nothing really sparks joy or sadness anymore. I just go through the motions at the café, serving coffee, but it feels like I’m watching someone else do it. Sleeping has been a nightmare too. I wake up constantly in the middle of the night, every single night, and it’s impossible to get back to sleep. I’ve lost so much weight, probably over 10 pounds in the last month, without even trying. Food just doesn't appeal to me.

But the worst part… I keep feeling things crawling on my skin, like tiny bugs, especially at night. And I know it sounds crazy, but I’m convinced it’s my fault the world is ending. Like, all the bad news on TV, the natural disasters… it’s because of something I did, or didn’t do. This awful feeling started alongside the numbness and the sleep problems, but even when those feelings lift a little, the crawling sensations and the guilt about the end of the world still stick around. They don’t just disappear.
D015-D005_h021.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Persistent Depressive Disorder

D015-D005_h025.question:
I'm just so tired, Doctor. It’s been about eight months now that this dark cloud has been following me everywhere. Even my husband, bless his heart, notices I'm just not myself. I feel this pervasive sadness, like a heavy blanket over everything. And the nightmares… they’re constant, vivid, and so disturbing that I dread falling asleep. Adding to that, I’ve put on a good amount of weight, probably over 5% in the last month alone, just no motivation to move or eat right. I feel so worthless, like I'm a burden to everyone around me.

But then there are these other things, too. There’s this man, a famous actor, I just know he’s in love with me. I get these strong feelings, like he’s sending me messages through the TV, little winks and subtle gestures meant only for me. And the tastes… sometimes I’ll be eating something normal, like toast, and it’ll taste like rust, or perfume. It’s so bizarre. What’s really strange is that these taste things, and the actor, they’ve been happening for a while even before I started feeling so down. I was still going to work every day, still managing, when these started coming up. Now, with everything else, it’s just overwhelming.
